### Coordinate splitting of submodules

`DifferentialOperatorSubmoduleSplitting.lean`:

- `projCoord` — a coordinate projection of `K[∂;δ]^ι`, as a left linear map;
- `exists_coord_generator` — the image of a submodule under a coordinate projection is a principal

This is the induction step of the structure theory of submodules of free modules over the operator
ring, hence of the diagonal reduction that identifies the cut invariant with the invariant-factor
vector.

### Generator count for submodules of a free module

`exists_generators_card_le`: a submodule of `K[∂;δ]^ι` supported on a finite set `t` of coordinates
is generated by at most `t.card` elements.  The induction peels one coordinate at a time with
`exists_coord_generator`, so no basis theory and no type-level index surgery is needed.

This is the noncommutative analogue of "a submodule of a free module over a principal ideal domain
is free of rank at most the rank", in the generator-count form that the diagonal reduction consumes.

### Quantitative torsion bound

`finrank_map_mkQ_le_sum_degree`: if a submodule is generated by a finite set `s` and each generator
`t` is carried into `L` by a nonzero operator `b t`, then

`dim_K (image of span s in the quotient by L) ≤ ∑_{t ∈ s} deg (b t)`.

The spanning set of the quotient image is `{∂^k · t : t ∈ s, k < deg (b t)}`, whose cardinality is
the right-hand side, so the bound follows from `finrank_span_finset_le_card`.

This upgrades the earlier finiteness statement to the quantitative form needed for the extremality
half of the identification of the cut invariant with the invariant-factor vector: it is the
inequality `dim_K (L ∩ V)/(M ∩ V) ≤ ∑ deg` in which the generators come from a cut.

### Explicit index bound

`OperatorLatticeIndexBound.lean` combines the two previous steps:

`finrank_quotient_le_card_mul` — if a lattice `N` is supported on `t` coordinates and every element
of `N` is carried into `L` by a nonzero operator of order at most `D`, then

`dim_K (N / L) ≤ t.card · D`.

This is the crude majorization behind the extremality of coordinate cuts: the number of generators
is bounded by the number of coordinates and each contributes at most `D` to the dimension.  The
sharp form, `∑_{i≤k} deg dᵢ` rather than `k · deg d₁`, needs the invariant-factor comparison and is
what still separates the cut invariant from the elementary-divisor vector.

### Two-sided Euclidean structure

`exists_left_div` (with `exists_leading_cancel_left`): for `b ≠ 0` every `a` can be written
`a = b * q + r` with `r = 0` or `deg r < deg b`.  The leading-term cancellation is the mirror of the
right-division one, using `leadCoeff (b * mono n c) = leadCoeff b * c`.

The operator ring is therefore Euclidean on both sides, which is what the column half of the
diagonal reduction needs: a column operation `colⱼ ← colⱼ + colⱼ₀ · q` reduces an entry modulo the
pivot on the right, so it consumes left division exactly as the row operations consume right
division.

### Row clearing by column operations

`DifferentialOperatorOreColumn.lean` now mirrors the row half of the reduction:

- `ColStep`, `ColEquiv`, with `ColEquiv.rowIndep` and `ColEquiv.boundedDistortion`;
- `exists_reduce_row` — left division against a pivot lowers every other entry of its row below the
  pivot order;
- `exists_pivot_clear_row` — a row with a nonzero entry can be cleared to a single pivot by column
  operations, by descent on the pivot order.

Both halves of the Jacobson reduction step are now available: `exists_pivot_clear` clears a column
with row operations and `exists_pivot_clear_row` clears a row with column operations.  What remains
is the interleaving (clearing a row may spoil the column, so the descent must run on the minimal
order of the whole matrix) and then the recursion on the complementary submatrix.

### The reduction step

`DifferentialOperatorOreReduction.lean`:

- `RowColStep`, `RowColEquiv`, with `RowColEquiv.of_rowEquiv`, `of_colEquiv` and `rowIndep`;
- **`exists_pivot_clear_both`** — every matrix with a nonzero entry is equivalent, under row and
  column operations, to one having a pivot which is the only nonzero entry of its row and of its
  column.

The descent runs on the order of the pivot.  One round of right division clears the pivot column;
one round of left division then clears the pivot row and, crucially, leaves the pivot column
untouched, because a column operation modifies only columns other than the pivot one — this is why
`exists_reduce_row` was strengthened to report that the whole pivot column is unchanged.  Whatever
survives has strictly smaller order and becomes the next pivot.

/-!
# Identifying the closure of a subspace by an orthogonality criterion

A subspace of a Hilbert space contained in a closed subspace has that closed subspace as its
closure exactly when no nonzero vector of the closed subspace is orthogonal to it.  The proof is
the orthogonal decomposition along the closure: the component orthogonal to the closure still lies
in the closed subspace, hence vanishes.

* `submodule_topologicalClosure_eq_of_orthogonal_inf_eq_bot`
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

variable {𝕜 E : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E]

/-- **A closed subspace whose intersection with the orthogonal complement of a subspace is trivial
is that subspace's closure.** -/
theorem submodule_topologicalClosure_eq_of_orthogonal_inf_eq_bot
    {K V : Submodule 𝕜 E} (hKV : K ≤ V) (hVc : IsClosed (V : Set E))
    (hbot : Kᗮ ⊓ V = ⊥) : K.topologicalClosure = V := by
  refine le_antisymm (K.topologicalClosure_minimal hKV hVc) fun a ha => ?_
  have hsup : K.topologicalClosure ⊔ K.topologicalClosureᗮ = ⊤ :=
    Submodule.sup_orthogonal_of_hasOrthogonalProjection
  have hmem : a ∈ K.topologicalClosure ⊔ K.topologicalClosureᗮ := by
    rw [hsup]
    exact Submodule.mem_top
  obtain ⟨p, hp, q, hq, hpq⟩ := Submodule.mem_sup.1 hmem
  have hpV : p ∈ V := K.topologicalClosure_minimal hKV hVc hp
  have hqV : q ∈ V := by
    have hqa : q = a - p := by
      rw [← hpq, add_sub_cancel_left]
    rw [hqa]
    exact V.sub_mem ha hpV
  have hqK : q ∈ Kᗮ := Submodule.orthogonal_le K.le_topologicalClosure hq
  have hq0 : q = 0 := by
    have hmem' : q ∈ Kᗮ ⊓ V := ⟨hqK, hqV⟩
    rwa [hbot, Submodule.mem_bot] at hmem'
  rw [← hpq, hq0, add_zero]
  exact hp

open scoped InnerProductSpace in
/-- **Orthogonality to a spanning set is orthogonality to the span.** -/
theorem mem_span_orthogonal {S : Set E} {x : E}
    (h : ∀ u ∈ S, (inner 𝕜 u x : 𝕜) = 0) : x ∈ (Submodule.span 𝕜 S)ᗮ := by
  rw [Submodule.mem_orthogonal]
  intro u hu
  induction hu using Submodule.span_induction with
  | mem y hy => exact h y hy
  | zero => rw [inner_zero_left]
  | add y z _ _ hy hz => rw [inner_add_left, hy, hz, add_zero]
  | smul c y _ hy => rw [inner_smul_left, hy, mul_zero]

# Subspaces associated with orthogonal projections

Here, the orthogonal projection is used to prove a series of more subtle lemmas about the
orthogonal complement of subspaces of `E` (the orthogonal complement itself was
defined in `Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Orthogonal.lean`) such that they admit
orthogonal projections; the lemma
`Submodule.sup_orthogonal_of_hasOrthogonalProjection`,
stating that for a subspace `K` of `E` such that `K` admits an orthogonal projection we have
`K ⊔ Kᗮ = ⊤`, is a typical example.
-/

variable {𝕜 E F : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜]

namespace Submodule

/-- If `K₁` admits an orthogonal projection and is contained in `K₂`,
then `K₁` and `K₁ᗮ ⊓ K₂` span `K₂`. -/
theorem sup_orthogonal_inf_of_hasOrthogonalProjection {K₁ K₂ : Submodule 𝕜 E} (h : K₁ ≤ K₂)
    [K₁.HasOrthogonalProjection] : K₁ ⊔ K₁ᗮ ⊓ K₂ = K₂ := by
  ext x
  rw [Submodule.mem_sup]
  let v : K₁ := orthogonalProjectionOnto K₁ x
  have hvm : x - v ∈ K₁ᗮ := sub_starProjection_mem_orthogonal x
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨y, hy, z, hz, rfl⟩
    exact K₂.add_mem (h hy) hz.2
  · exact fun hx => ⟨v, v.prop, x - v, ⟨hvm, K₂.sub_mem hx (h v.prop)⟩, add_sub_cancel _ _⟩

variable {K} in
/-- If `K` admits an orthogonal projection, then `K` and `Kᗮ` span the whole space. -/
theorem sup_orthogonal_of_hasOrthogonalProjection [K.HasOrthogonalProjection] : K ⊔ Kᗮ = ⊤ := by
  convert Submodule.sup_orthogonal_inf_of_hasOrthogonalProjection (le_top : K ≤ ⊤)
  simp

/-- If `K` admits an orthogonal projection, then the orthogonal complement of its orthogonal
complement is itself. -/
@[simp]
theorem orthogonal_orthogonal [K.HasOrthogonalProjection] : Kᗮᗮ = K := by
  ext v
  constructor
  · obtain ⟨y, hy, z, hz, rfl⟩ := K.exists_add_mem_mem_orthogonal v
    intro hv
    have hz' : z = 0 := by
      have hyz : ⟪z, y⟫ = 0 := by simp [hz y hy, inner_eq_zero_symm]
      simpa [inner_add_right, hyz] using hv z hz
    simp [hy, hz']
  · intro hv w hw
    rw [inner_eq_zero_symm]
    exact hw v hv

lemma orthogonal_le_orthogonal_iff {K₀ K₁ : Submodule 𝕜 E} [K₀.HasOrthogonalProjection]
    [K₁.HasOrthogonalProjection] : K₀ᗮ ≤ K₁ᗮ ↔ K₁ ≤ K₀ :=
  ⟨fun h ↦ by simpa using orthogonal_le h, orthogonal_le⟩

lemma orthogonal_le_iff_orthogonal_le {K₀ K₁ : Submodule 𝕜 E} [K₀.HasOrthogonalProjection]
    [K₁.HasOrthogonalProjection] : K₀ᗮ ≤ K₁ ↔ K₁ᗮ ≤ K₀ := by
  rw [← orthogonal_le_orthogonal_iff, orthogonal_orthogonal]

lemma le_orthogonal_iff_le_orthogonal {K₀ K₁ : Submodule 𝕜 E} [K₀.HasOrthogonalProjection]
    [K₁.HasOrthogonalProjection] : K₀ ≤ K₁ᗮ ↔ K₁ ≤ K₀ᗮ := by
  rw [← orthogonal_le_orthogonal_iff, orthogonal_orthogonal]

/-- In a Hilbert space, the orthogonal complement of the orthogonal complement of a subspace `K`
is the topological closure of `K`.

Note that the completeness assumption is necessary. Let `E` be the space `ℕ →₀ ℝ` with inner space
structure inherited from `PiLp 2 (fun _ : ℕ ↦ ℝ)`. Let `K` be the subspace of sequences with the sum
of all elements equal to zero. Then `Kᗮ = ⊥`, `Kᗮᗮ = ⊤`. -/
theorem orthogonal_orthogonal_eq_closure [CompleteSpace E] :
    Kᗮᗮ = K.topologicalClosure := by
  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
  · convert Submodule.orthogonal_orthogonal_monotone K.le_topologicalClosure
    rw [K.topologicalClosure.orthogonal_orthogonal]
  · exact K.topologicalClosure_minimal K.le_orthogonal_orthogonal Kᗮ.isClosed_orthogonal

  refine ⟨?_, fun h => by rw [h, Submodule.top_orthogonal_eq_bot]⟩

    simp only [restrict_apply, domRestrict_apply]

  refine IsCompl.of_eq this (eq_top_of_finrank_eq <| (finrank_le _).antisymm ?_)

  rw [← finrank_bot K V, ← this, finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq,
    finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal b₁]
  exact le_self_add
